history.summary: Maa Madwarani Mandir is a well-known hilltop Shakti shrine in Korba district, regarded locally as a major centre of faith. According to the Korba district administration, the temple of Goddess Madwarani stands on a hill beside the Korba-Champa Road, about 22 km from the district headquarters; the local legend says that during the Navratri season, jowar (sorghum) grows under the Kalmi trees near the temple, and a fair is celebrated by local people every year in the Navratri season. The temple is reached by both stairs and road and is thronged by thousands of devotees during Navratri. Coordinates are a village-level estimate and are APPROXIMATE (unverified against a map pin).

name: Mandwarani Temple
town_description: TOWN CORRECTED: the CSV lists 'Korba', but the temple is at the village of Madwarani on the Korba-Champa Road in Kartala tehsil, roughly 20-22 km from Korba city, near the villages of Kharhari and Rampur. The settlement is best known for the hilltop Maa Madwarani Mandir, one of the district's principal Shakti shrines, which hosts a large Navratri fair each year. The surrounding area is rural and forested, and the temple hill offers views over the countryside.
